Commentary.Commentary: Dale Steyn and Kagiso Rabada snared three wickets apiece as the duo gave the Kiwi batsmen a real work over. Vernon Philander was decent as well. The hosts bowlers were relentless in their accuracy. They have a sizeable 267-run lead but SOUTH AFRICA HAVE NOT ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON. Join us in a while for the final session of the day.

That brings the New Zealand innings to a close. Barring their skipper Kane Williamson who played brilliantly, none of the visiting batsmen showed enough spunk on a track that had just enough in it for the pacers. Williamson looked assured in his stay and was the last man out. Henry Nicholls got a start but couldn't convert while Neil Wagner struck a few lusty blows towards the end.

OUT! Edged and taken! It's all over for New Zealand! Short of a length delivery on off, Willimason looks to pull but only manages to get an outside edge towards de Kock who doesn't miss many. A fighting innings from the Kiwi skipper comes to an end. NEW ZEALAND BOWLED OUT FOR 214 AND TRAIL BY 267 RUNS! EARLY TEA HAS ALSO BEEN TAKEN.
Fuller and on the pads, Kane flicks it towards square leg. The fielder takes his own time to collect the ball. So, Willimason has decided he will face most of the deliveries.
Short and angled on the pads, Williamson flicks it towards backward square leg and doesn't want a single.
CLOSE SHAVE! Slower and fuller on leg stump, Boult makes room to flick but misses. The ball just went past the leg stump.
TRENT BOULT is the last man in!

OUT! STEYN HAS THE LAST LAUGH! It's the short ball that works eventually! Dug in short outside off, Wagner backs away to pull and gets a thin edge through to de Kock who takes it with ease. Steyn is pumped up and gives the southpaw a real send off. Ends a really entertaining cameo from Wagner.
Shortish outside off, punched off the back foot to the covers.
That's yet another bouncer around off, Wagner doesn't connect on the pull and gets a verbal piece of advice from Steyn. Let's hope that was a clean formal chat.
FOUR! SMASHED! This short ball ploy is now getting tiresome from the Proteas. Another bumper around off, Wagner stays back and blasts the pull through square leg. That rocketed to the fence.
Short ball on middle and off, Wagner backs away to pull it away but misses.
Good length down the leg side, Kane misses the flick.
FOUR! CLASSY SHOT! Fuller outside off, Williamson leans forward to that one and drives it beautifully straight back past the bowler down the ground to the fence for a boundary.
WAGNER SURVIVES! Length ball outside off, pushed to mid on for a quick single. Van Zyl's throw at the bowler's end misses as otherwise the southpaw would have been gone.
Fullish and wide outside off, Wagner isn't backing away from playing shots and tries to go big down the ground. Miscues it but has enough on it to get it over mid on. A brace taken.
Length ball outside off, punched off the back foot to mid on for a single.
Good length outside off, blocked off the back foot to short mid-wicket.

FOUR! CLOBBERED! Shortish around leg stump, Wagner shuffles across and shovels this uppishly over the infield.  In the air and there was a deep mid-wicket in place but gets it well to the left of the fielder to find the fence.
Another bouncer and this time Wagner misses the pull. Steyn got the height right this time.
Wagner is having a change of bat.

FOUR! IN THE AIR...BUT SAFE! One more to the bouncer list and Wagner responds with another pull. Not in control this time and gets a top edge that flies over the slip cordonm to the ropes. Seems to have broken his bat in the process.
There's a deep mid-wicket in place now.
SIX! THAT'S EVEN BIGGER! Another short ball around off, Wagner is hanging back expecting the bouncer and absolutely nails the pull this time. Sends it soaring over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
FOUR! KABOOM! Wagner has had enough of the short ball treatment! Dug in short around off, camps back and pulls it ferociously over mid-wicket. Made clean contact.
Dug in short outside off, Wagner shapes himself for the wild pull but misses.
DALE STEYN is back on.
Full toss outside off, Wagner bunts it through mid off as the ball goes to the deep before it is pulled back in. Three more added.
Drifting on to the pads, worked away to the leg side for a single.

SIX! THAT FLEW OFF THE BLADE! Short ball around off, Williamson goes for the pull off the front foot but hasn't controlled it at all. Doesn't matter though as the ball flies way over long leg for a maximum.

NOT OUT! Fuller around leg stump, Wagner goes across to flick but is hit on the pads. Appeal for lbw but not given. SA decide to gamble with the review. It's a legal ball but has pitched outside leg. So that's the end of that. SA have lost both their reviews. The batsmen had crossed over and no signal from the umpire, so there must have been an inside edge.
An LBW decision is taken upstairs.
Another crackling bouncer and Wagner just about ducks under it.

No ball! NOT OUT! What a ball though! Fired in short around leg stump, Wagner tries to take evasive action as the ball lobs up for a while. Faf from second slip charges forward to take it nicely. The appeal for a catch is given but Wagner is adamant that he hasn't hit it. He opts for the review. It seems like Rabada has overstepped and so that's a no ball. We don't even have to go further with the review process. As it turns out, the ball had come off the shoulder, so a good review from Neil.
Wagner has been given out off a snorter from Rabada. He opts for the review.
Dug in short around off, Wagner ducks under it just in time. Ripper!
Fuller on middle and off, worked to mid-wicket for a single.
Slider well outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Drifting in from outside off, blocked nicely from the crease.
Slider outside off, blocked off the back foot to cover.
Flatter around off, defended well from the crease.
Flatter on middle and leg, worked off the back foot through square leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Wagner flashes at it and is beaten.
Back of a length angled away from just outside off, Wagner almost plays at it and withdraws his bat at the very last moment. Lucky not to get a nick.
Dug in short again around off, angled away as Wagner sways away from the line in time.

Very full and wide outside off, the sucker ball and Wagner falls into the trap as he has a go at it. The ball lobs to Amla at first slip who collects it and appeals for a catch. The umpires aren't sure and they want to refer it with the third umpire. Seemed like a bump ball in real motion and replays confirm the same.
South Africa are appealing for a catch at first slip. Seems like a bump ball though and the umpires want to check it upstairs to be sure.
Another short ball around leg stump, this time Wagner ducks under it with ease.
Wagner is hit on the helmet and the grill of his helmet comes out. My colleague sitting next to me says, "Is Wagner getting a taste of his own medicine?"

Short of a length delivery on middle, Wagner looks to duck but ball didn't bounce much and hits him on the grill of the helmet. At the same time, the replays are being shown where Wagner did the same thing to Rabada during the Durban Test.
Loopy ball around off, pushed through covers for a single.
NEIL WAGNER is the new man in!

OUT! Edged and gone! de Kock takes a sharp catch and Piedt gets his first! Gives this one a bit more flight and bowls it around off, Southee makes room to cut but this time the ball kisses the outside edge of his bat and de Kock behind the stumps takes a superb catch. Southee walks back and Williamson is really running out of partners here.
A loud shout for lbw, but was pitched outside leg! Loopy ball around leg, Southee looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. An lbw appeal is made but the umpire shakes his head.
Beaten up! Gives this one a bit more air and throws it outside off, it skids after pitching too as Southee goes for a cut shot but gets beaten.
Flattish on middle, punched off the back foot towards mid on.
Tossed up around off, from round the wicket. Driven down to long off for a single.

Rabada this time bowls a fullish delivery and aims the middle and leg stump, Southee stays back and swings his bat hard at this. Gets a good enough connection on it and sends the ball towards deep mid-wicket. Van Zyl out in the deep runs to his left and puts in a good dive to keep the ball from the ropes. Two runs are taken and that's the end of an eventful over from Kagiso Rabada.

It's for sure now, Southee has been given his orders. Length ball angling in on middle and leg, Tim goes for the big pull over mid-wicket. Once again, misses the shot completely as the ball just goes over the stumps.
Length ball on middle stump, it's turned towards mid-wicket for a run by Kane Williamson.
Fired in full outside off, Tim Southee reaches out to this to play at it. Gets it off the toe end of the bat as the ball rolls away down towards third man. One run taken.

SWING AND A MISS! Seems Southee's going for it here. Get in as many as possible. It's on a length and outside off, shaping in too, Tim stands back and looks to whack it through the off side. Misses it completely though as the keeper collects it.

FOUR! EDGED AND AWAY! How did that go by? Tim Southee with one of the most awkward looking shots there. It's pitched just back of a length and way outside off, Southee walks across a long way to try and paddle it initially, but then realizes that he can't do that and is all squared up. Lifts his bat to defend as the ball takes a thick outside edge. Flies past the man at third slip and beats the fielder at third man as well. Gets a boundary when he really should have been out.
FOUR! Too easy for Kane! Loopy delivery around leg, Williamson just helps it on its way down to fine leg for another boundary. 10 from the over!
On middle and leg, swept straight to the man at square leg. Good stop by the fielder there, otherwise it would have been another boundary.
Flattish on middle, flicked through backward square leg for an easy brace.

FOUR! Nicely swept! Loopy delivery around middle and leg, Williamson senses it early, gets down on one knee and sweeps it off the meat of the bat towards fine leg for a boundary. That sped away to the fence in no time. Williamson doing the right thing, trying to score as much as possible.
Tossed up around off, turns in after pitching. Williamson looks to flick it across the line but misses and is hit on the pads.
Loopy ball around middle and off, Williamson makes a watchful leave.
Gets behind the line and defends it down.
Southee gets forward and drives it towards mid off.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Tim ducks in sanity.
Good length delivery on off, punched off the back foot towards covers.

DROPPED! A caught and bowled chance goes abegging. Rabada didn't expect this one. He bowls a length delivery on off, Southee makes room and ends up hitting it back to the bowler. Rabada in his followthrough looks to grab but the ball bursts off his palms, he then looks to take it in the second attempt but fails to cling onto it. Should have been taken.
On a length and around middle, Southee looks to defend but gets beaten and is hit on the pads.
22nd Test fifty for Kane Williamson!

FOUR! BEAUTIFUL SHOT! Williamson making great use of his feet there. It's flighted well on middle and off, Kane is quick to act on this. Gets to the pitch of the delivery and lofts it over the mid-wicket region. Gets enough on it and as there's no protection in the deep, the ball races away to the boundary line. Brings up his fifty as well with that shot and it's been a good knock here so far.
Full and attacking the stumps, Tim eases it down to long on for one run.
Looped up by Dane Piedt this time, on middle and leg and gives it some flight as well, it's flicked to mid-wicket.
Dane tosses it up on off stump, Southee plants his front foot forward and blocks it to the right of the bowler.
Loopy off-spinner on middle and leg, it's turned through backward square leg for a single.
Piedt tosses it up on middle and leg, turning in, it's worked in front on forward short leg.
Full on leg, Southee looks to play it but is struck on the pads.
TIM SOUTHEE is the next batsman in.

OUT! LBW! Deadly accurate! Rabada's plan works. After pitching the ball on the pads, he changes things up and sends in a fuller delivery around off. Bracewell plays it safe, stepping forward and looking to defend it with a straight bat. The ball has other ideas as it takes off after the bounce and swings into his pads. That was dead plump and Bracewell has no hope. The umpire raises his finger, and Bracewell looks to Williamson. The skipper shakes his head and decides not to review it. NZ are in serious trouble!
Fuller delivery on middle and leg, defended from within the crease.
Back of a length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Fuller delivery on off, driven through mid on.

FOUR! TEASER! Fuller ball on the pads, Bracewell works it neatly through the leg side. Philander at deep mid-wicket chases it and the ball keeps him running till the end but the ball crosses the ropes.
KAGISO RABADA to bowl.
Wide down the leg side, Bracewell goes after it and is hit on the pads. The batsmen run a single and the umpire signals a bye.
FOUR! Down the ground! Bracewell is growing in confidence here. Full delivery outside off, Bracewell strides forward and drives it sharply past the bowler and through mid off to find the boundary.
Tossed up ball, defended back to the bowler.
Landed on middle and leg, Bracewell flicks it to the leg side. It just misses hitting the legs of Temba Bavuma at short leg and goes on to square leg.
Flighted on middle, tucked to square leg.
Served on the stumps, flicked to the leg side.
DANE PIEDT is back on.
Shorter ball outside off, Williamson stands back in the crease and blocks it to the off side.
Fullish delivery outside off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
In the channel outside off, Williamson steps across but chooses to leave it.
Length ball on leg, worked to point for a single.
Fuller ball around off, Bracewell defends it off the front foot back to the bowler.
BEATEN! Length delivery that looks to be swinging away, Bracewell steps forward and looks to push it. The ball shapes in and just about beats the inside edge of the bat and goes to the keeper.
Back of a length delivery outside off, KW rises and taps it down into the track besides him. That'll be the end of the over.
Steyn pitches this a tad full, just outside off and there's some movement away this time. Williamson comes forward, but leaves it alone yet again.
Length delivery outside off, Kane Williamson being as watchful as ever, lets it be.
Leg bye! Aiming the hips here, Bracewell looks to flick this away but the ball goes off his thigh pad. A leg bye is taken as the ball rolls over to the leg side.
Good length ball around off, it's pushed towards wide mid off for nothing.
Steyn comes steaming in, bowls it too straight though. It's on middle and leg and Williamson just tucks it through the mid-wicket region for a single.

FOUR! Edged and away! Would be a little frustrating for the Proteas but still, positive signs. Back of a length delivery outside off, Doug Bracewell has a poke at this and gets a thick outside edge. It flies between gully and backward point and races away to the fence as the fielders can only watch that.
Keeps it on a length here, just around the off stump, Bracewell blocks it off his back foot.
On a good length and outside off, the Kiwi skipper opens the face of the bat and runs it down to third man for an easy single.

FOUR! Excellent shot. The balance on that shot was perfect as he played it. Short delivery just outside off, Williamson picks up the length early. Gets himself into position early and with a nice, steady head, pulls this between mid-wicket and mid on to send it all the way to the boundary line.
Fullish in length and pitched outside off, Kane prods forward and blocks it with a solid straight bat.
Good length delivery on middle, tucked towards the right of the bowler.
Short of a length ball on off, Bracewell gets back to defend but gets an outside edge which falls safely in front of the man at gully.
Another shortish ball on middle, Bracewell ducks to evade it.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Doug crouches under it.
Full length delivery on off, moving away nicely with some good pace on it. Bracewell leaves it alone.
Good length ball on off, punched off the back foot towards covers.

Back of a length delivery on off, Williamson hops and guides it through cover-point for a single. South Africa are happy as long as he is away from the strike. They want the new batsman to face as many balls.
DALE STEYN to bowl from the other end!
Strays it down the leg side, Bracwell looks to flick it but fails to do so.
Touch full and going away a bit, it's well defended off the front foot by Doug.
FOUR! Delightful stroke! Fuller length delivery on off, was asking to be driven. Bracewell accepts the proposal and creams it past the man at mid off for a boundary. First runs of the session, then.
Short of a length ball on off, Doug gets back and punches it straight to the man at covers.
Beaten! On a length and outside off, Bracewell looks to push it through the cover but the ball shapes away and he gets beaten up.

NOT OUT! The decision stays as it is! Philander comes running in and hurls it on leg, Bracewell looks to flick it across the line but misses and is hit on the pads. They all go up in an appeal but the umpire says not out. Faf once again opts to take the review and replays show it was in line but was going on to clip the leg stick.
An LBW review is taken straightway by the Proteas. Will it be successful again?

Welcome back for the afternoon session! The Kiwis have an uphill task ahead of them and will be banking heavily on their skipper now. KANE WILLIAMSON and DOUG BRACEWELL to continue. VERNON PHILANDER will steam in first up. Let's play...
...DAY 3, SESSION 2...

South Africa will be really happy as they have been successful in reversing both the decisions and will go into lunch with smiles on their faces. How long can the Kiwi tail wag? Will South Africa enforce the follow-on if they clean them up early? All your questions will be answered soon. Join us back in a very short while.

Williamson is still holding one end but is running out of partners. Henry Nicholls showed some promise at the start but was removed by some pure pace by Rabada. Watling didn't last long and just minutes before lunch, Philander sent Santner back for a duck.

This session - 24 overs, 80 runs and 3 wickets! Another session going bravely in the favour of South Africa. Though they failed to create any impact in the first hour of play, they came back roaring in the second half. The pacers have scalped 3 wickets and have thrown the Kiwis in dire straits now, trailing by a mammoth 363 runs.

Lands it full around off, straightening a touch, Bracewell tries to defend by getting across the stumps and it goes off the outside part of the bat. It rolls in the gap at covers and they collect a single. LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Full length ball on off, an outswinger, Bracewell covers the line and shoulders arms.
Good length ball on middle, Bracewell goes on the back foot and defends it off his pads to the leg side.
Bouncer around off, easily ducked by Bracewell. Expect a yorker any time now.
On a length around off, Bracewell defends it from within the crease.

FIVE WIDES! Steyn digs in a short ball but it troubles his keeper more than the batsman. Bracewell easily ducks and de Kock uses every inch of his height to stop the ball. But only manages fingertips to it.
Good length ball on middle, tapped in the gap on the leg side for a single.
Movement back into the batsman, from around off, Bracewell fails to defend off his front foot and is hit high on the front pad. A stifled appeal dies immediately.
Pitches it full and on off, Bracewell gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Doug Bracewell walks in next.

OUT! Timbaahhh... Philander strikes just before lunch and New Zealand are pushed in a corner now. It's a length ball around middle and off, 136.3 kph, Santner with no footwork tries to defend but it catches the inside edge of the bat, brushes his pads and cannons onto the stumps. Santner bags a duck. New Zealand trail by 370 runs.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Philander angles across a length ball outside off, Williamson allows it through.
Williamson has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR BYES! Steyn bangs in a short ball and Santner ducks. de Kock attempts to collect it but fails to do so. Bonus runs for New Zealand.
Short ball outside off, Santner sways away from the line.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Santner leaves it alone.
Mitchell Santner is in next.

OUT! It's gloved. Steyn lets out yet another short ball around leg, Watling fends at it and it seems it has gone off his gloves to the keeper. de Kock collects the ball and appeals, Steyn joins him a bit late but the umpire shakes his head. Faf du Plessis immediately opts for the review and the replays confirm the involvement of the gloves. Watling has to walk back and it's a big blow to New Zealand. They trail by 375 runs. This is also Steyn's 50th Test wicket in Centurion.
Shout for a catch! Not given by the umpire and South Africa take the referral.
A touch short and around off, Williamson jumps on the back foot and turns it through square leg for a single.
Steyn bangs in a bouncer around leg, 138.5 kph, Williamson sits underneath it.
On a length and outside off, Watling gets across the stumps a bit and shoulders arms.
Full and on off, Watling flicks it off his front foot to the leg side. Not in the gap.
Good length ball outside off, moving away a bit, Watling shoulders arms.
Full and straight, shaping in a shade, Watling plays it from his pads to the leg side.

Philander serves a full ball on off, Watling plays a confident cover drive but finds the fielder. Philander is not as quick as Rabada and hence he allows some extra time to the batsmen to play their preferred shots.
Full in length and outside off, Williamson pushes it towards cover-point for a single.
Vernon Philander replaces Rabada in the attack. One final burst for him before lunch.
We are getting the confirmation from the ground that DRS is now working from both ends. Earlier it was down on the Hennops River End from where umpire Ian Gould is officiating.
Another bouncer, this time there is ample bounce to take the ball over the batsman. Watling ducks.

That's dangerous on this pitch! Steyn bangs in a short ball around leg, BJ looks to duck but the ball doesn't bounce much and nearly hits the batsman on the body. It's a good take by Quinton behind the stumps.
Shortish and slower in pace, down the leg side, Watling takes his body away from the line and leaves it alone.

Excellent delivery, full and outside off, shaping away, Watling allows it through safely. There was this temptation of going for a booming cover drive but the Kiwi wicketkeeper knows the need of hour.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Watling could have left it but he decides to play it away from his body. Taps it down to the off side and shouts "no" as his partner was interested in a run.

Wrong line by Steyn, it's on back of a length and around the hips of Williamson, who glances it  through backward square leg for a single. Thinks about the second run but the fielder in the deep is quickly to the ball.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Watling chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Beauty by Rabada! He gets a length ball to straighten a bit from around off, Watling is caught pushing and missing inside the line.

FOUR! Lovely stroke to bring up New Zealand's 100! Rabada angles in a full ball on middle, Watling meets it with a straight bat, good positive front foot movement and he times his drive to perfection. The placement is exquisite as well and it races away to the fence at long on.
Bowls it on a fuller length and outside off, Watling gets forward and then leaves it alone.
Fullish and angling in, 148.1 kph, Williamson nudges it on the leg side and crosses.

FIVE RUNS! Rabada follows up the full ball with a bouncer but it goes way over the batsman and the keeper. de Kock tries his level best to stop the ball with a jump but it brushes his gloves and screams away to the fence.
Rabada attempts for a yorker but ends up slipping a full toss on off, quite sharp in pace, Williamson only manages to dig it out to mid on.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Angles in a full ball on off, 136 kph, Watling covers the line and defends.
Shortish and on off, Williamson goes back and punches it in the gap on the off side. Good enough for a single.
Steyn hurls in a length ball in the corridor of uncertainty, Williamson shoulders arms.
Full and angling down the leg side, Williamson goes for an instinctive flick shot but fails to connect.
Back of a length ball on off, Williamson defends it from the crease.
Dale Steyn to speed in from the other end.
Nearly chops it on! A pacey delivery, 145 kph, Watling goes to defend but it takes the toe end of the bat and almost disturbed the stumps.
Fuller and on off, driven off the front foot to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Rabada keeps his line straight and length full, Williamson pushes it past his partner at the other end and crosses for a single.
Arrows in a full ball on off, Williamson gets behind the line and defends it to the leg side. Was hurried up due to the excessive pace and fullish length.
Beauty of a delivery! Rabada dishes out a fuller length ball outside off, it holds its line after landing, Williamson gets forward to defend but is beaten comprehensively.
Slower through the air this time, once again Watling does well to defend it with soft hands to the leg side.
Flighted on middle, defended on the leg side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot.

EDGED AND FOUR! Not a convincing way to get off the mark for BJ! Loopy ball around off, not turning much, Watling gets forward to defend but it catches the outside edge and speeds past first slip for a boundary.
Tossed up ball on off, Watling defends it from the crease to the leg side.
Spinning into the batsman from a full length around off, Williamson gets forward and turns it past short leg for a run.
A bouncer to greet the new batsman, outside off, Watling ducks underneath it. End of an impressive over, a wicket maiden.
BJ Watling walks in next.

OUT! The decision is overturned. It's dead plumb in front of the wickets. Rabada strikes and his pace has done the trick. Spears in a full ball in the line of the stumps, 145.6 kph, Nicholls is caught napping inside the crease as he tries to play across the line. He is beaten for pace and is rapped on the back pad. They appeal, the umpire disagrees and South Africa quickly take the DRS. The replays show that it has landed on leg and would have gone on to destroy the stumps. Finally a breakthrough for the Proteas this morning. The change in field probably was playing in Nicholls' mind as he was expecting a short ball after a leg slip and fly slip were placed prior to this ball. But it was a double bluff from Kagiso. Smart planning. New Zealand trail by 395 runs.
Appeal for an lbw. That looks dead plumb to the naked eye but the umpire shakes his head. South Africa immediately take the review...
Change in field. A leg slip comes in place and there is a fly slip as well.
This is seriously big pace. Rabada clocks 150.2 kph and lands a length ball around middle and leg. Nicholls once again gets hurried up and takes a blow on his arm.
Slips a length ball down the leg side, Nicholls tries to flick but misses.

Ooohhh...another nervous moment for Henry. Rabada bangs in a short ball, 146.8 kph, Nicholls goes back, is hurried up by the pace and then tries to keep it out. But the ball catches the outside half of the bat and drops wide of Bavuma at short leg.

Nearly carries to short leg! Sharp length ball around leg, Nicholls tries working it off his pads but it takes the inside edge and goes a bit aerially to the left of Bavuma. He reacts but the ball is too far.
Tossed up ball on off, it's defended off the front foot and with the spin to the leg side. 7 runs off the over, a wayward start from Piedt.
Another long hop by Piedt, Nicholls gets back and pulls it through backward square leg for three runs.
Flighted and on off, played with the spin to point.
Better line and length, a tossed up ball outside off, spinning away, Nicholls covers his stumps and shoulders arms.

FOUR! Pushing his luck too much there, Piedt. Once again he drags his length short and plants it outside off, Nicholls this time goes deep inside the crease and whacks it through point for a boundary.
It's a gentle loosener first up from the offie, short and around off, Nicholls goes back to pull but finds the mid-wicket fielder. Dane was really lucky there.
Spin introduced straightaway after the drinks break. It will be Dane Piedt to roll his arm. Let's see if he can get some turn from the pitch or not. A slip and deepish short leg in place.

Drinks are on the field! A good first hour for the Kiwis. They have dealt nicely with the Protea pace attack and another good thing coming their way was a solid 50-run stand between Williamson and Nicholls. Faf du Plessis will be kicking himself for dropping his counterpart. Will it prove costly? Can the duo see off the morning session? Let's wait and find out.
Length delivery on off, defended towards covers for a single.
Fuller length delivery on off, Nicholls drives it hard but finds the man at covers.
Length ball on off, Henry is happy to not go after it.
In the corridor of uncertainty, HN makes a watchful leave.
50-run stand between Williamson and Nicholls!
FOUR! On the pads and Nicholls won't let that go waste. He quickly gets across and flicks it beautifully through backward square leg for a boundary.
Rabada comes from round the wicket, bangs it short and outside off, pretty much a harmless ball. It's been left alone.
Covers the line and defends it gently towards covers.
Good length ball on off, played towards point.
Fuller length ball on off, Nicholls looks to defend but gets an inside edge past the leg stump for a single towards fine leg.
"Rabada from South Africa is a quality bowler, he will enjoy bowling in Australia this summer and make the Aussie boys jump around !", tweets a concerned Shane Warne.
Back of a length ball outside off, punched sweetly through covers and got an easy couple.
On a length and around off, easy leave for Henry.
Comes from round the wicket and bowls it wide outside off, the batsman doesn't fiddle with it.
FOUR! Cut away and it will go for a boundary! Short of a length outside off, Williamson cuts it through gully and point for a boundary. It was placed perfectly in the gap.
Fuller length delivery on middle, Williamson walks across to flick but gets a leading edge back to the bowler.
On a length and curls in this time, Kane gets back and keeps it out on the off side.
Touch full and around off, defended back to the bowler.
A length delivery angled on middle, worked away on the leg side for a single.
Bowls it short and around middle, at 146.4 kph, Nicholls looks to flick but is beaten by the pace there. The ball hits him on the thigh pad and lobs towards the slip cordon.

We are all set for the action to begin. The umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. KANE WILLIAMSON and HENRY NICHOLLS will continue from where they left off yesterday. DALE STEYN to start off with the bowling proceedings with three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

New Zealand have lost three critical wickets already and their fate now rests on Kane Williamson's shoulders. This session will be crucial to the match as South Africa will come out looking to take a couple of quick wickets. With only two batsmen of quality to follow in Watling and Santner, Williamson and Nicholls will have to hold steady and ride out the very really possibility of a batting collapse. It is a bright and sunny day over SuperSport Park, Centurion, so stay tuned for a cracker of a day.

Hello and welcome to the 3rd Day of the final Test of the series between South Africa and New Zealand. South Africa have been in complete control of the game so far with Faf du Plessis steering them to an enourmous lead of 481. It is a do-or-die day for the tourists as the Proteans will be gunning for them from the moment they step on the field.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

So at the end of two days, South Africa are well on top, with a lead of 443, needing 7 wickets to wrap things up in the first innings. Will we see a rearguard action from the visitors? Or will the home side run through its opposition? Join us tomorrow at 1330 IST (0800 GMT) for all the action from Day 3. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

It all depends on Kane Williamson and how he fights tomorrow and whether the team can rally around him. Yes, Santner can bat, so can Watling but this is a tall ask. Earlier today, Faf du Plessis scored a Test ton after nearly 2 years to revive his career and also put his side well on top. He will be relishing the opportunity tomorrow of bowling out the Black Caps inside two sessions and may be, even enforce the follow-on.

A disastrous day for New Zealand. If yesterday was bad, today was worse. The Proteas piled on 481 and in reply, the tourists have already lost 3 wickets. With an inexperienced middle order to follow, things do not look too bright for the Kiwis. Neil Wagner was the only shining star, with a 5-wicket haul.

OUT! Taylor is gone. He pushed this towards short mid-wicket and set off for what he though was a single available. However, Williamson thought otherwise as he saw the dynamite Temba Bavuma lurking at short leg. He sent Taylor back and Bavuma charged to the ball, picked it up had a shy at the striker's end and bingo! Taylor tried to stretch but he knew he was gone. He started walking to the dressing room straightaway and just stopped for a brief moment at the boundary line, awaiting the third umpire's call. Once that came, he was off. Replays clearly showed he was well short. NEW ZEALAND STILL TRAIL BY 455 RUNS.
